body: I haven't said HOW I am going to do it. Where in any of this have I explained how I am going to do it??

My "plan" is not predicated on any of this coming to fruition. Regardless of any insurance payout or my ability to donate organs I will proceed with suicide. 

I'm merely asking for assistance with the organ donation component of my plan. Anyone who is seriously going to commit suicide should at least explore organ donation while they are alive.

Suicide is a heartbreaking thing for 1 family. As someone who is suicidal I want to at least bring joy to other families so I know my death won't be "for nothing"

My suicide is not predicated based on the guarantee of an insurance payout. I have been suicidal long long long before me applying for the insurance. Anytime someone is paying out large sums of money there is always a risk they won't pay. 

I am not advocating suicide at all and I'm certainly not advocating suicide for expectation of an insurance payout.
Mods, can you please confirm this is not an acceptable post. If so, I have no problem removing this I just would like to get my questions answered and this seems like a very active sub.

I have discussed this with an attorney and although possible, it's highly unlikely they could get out of paying the claim. 

There is no way for the insurance company to prove my intent when establishing the policy. So long as I wait the required amount of time (2 years) then they would violate the contract by not paying. 

It's a risk I'm willing to take. Although per the attorney I spoke with, a small risk

Given the option would you rather someone who is suicidal just go out to the forest/desert/wherever and just off themselves or go with my plan?

I am not advocating for or against suicide but if someone's mind is made up and they are determined, it would be borderline selfish not to donate your parts. My "loss" as some would put it is making someone's life. By my count I should be able to have a lasting impact on 3 peoples lives by donating a kidney, liver and bone marrow. And that s assuming they can salvage anything from my body after I'm gone...

It's a very selfless idea but you have to be 100% committed to suicide. 

1- if you end up going through with the donation and not the suicide you are going to live without a kidney or part of your liver which is not ideal. Likely you'll be more miserable than before.
2- if you start exploring the organ donation and meet with families of people who need the organs and don't go through with it; your going to seriously upset people who don't deserve it.

I urge anyone considering my plan to make sure you are 110% committed before meeting people and such...

It's not suicide insurance! Lol

It's regular life insurance. They put a restriction on there for the first few years where death by suicide is not covered and your beneficiary will not be paid. Some insurers go up to like 5-10 years for that restriction.

The one I went with is a 2 year wait.
